This is Barry the giant sea worm, who in 2009 was discovered living in a coral tank in the Blue Reef Aquarium in Cornwall, England. He had been accidentally imported as a larva, and grew to enormous size in the predator-free environment.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There is some vital information missing here. Most importantly, are the contained specimens the only population, or are there others loose in the world? Is there a MTF assigned to locate any un-contained instances? How many individuals are in containment? Do they breed in captivity, and if not, what conditions are required for reproduction? If the animal can bore through windows and walls, what is the extent of this ability? Is brick enough to keep them out? Can they penetrate certain metals?

A big smart sneaky bug that eats your children is creepy, but I feel that there is a lot needed to make this a technical document on the containment of a dangerous, anomalous species.

I think you have completely failed to grasp the concept of object classes. It's safe because we can reliably contain it. If we keep it in a live containment vault with appropriate countermeasures, it can't do anything, it is contained and is thus safe.

Object classes aren't about danger, they're about containment.
